guard: a smoke broker owned through the helper dies when its suite is SIGNALLED, not only when the suite returns
why: ONE MUTATION, AND IT REINSTATES THE OBSERVED DEFECT. Narrowing the registered signals to SIGHUP
leaves the helper's structure, its exit handler, and its bookkeeping intact while removing the
only thing that fires when a seat is killed. That is precisely the state the tree was in when a
signalled bind-fence left broker pid 150309 alive, reparented to ppid 1, port still bound.
THE SUITE'S OWN POSITIVE CONTROL IS WHY THE KILL MEANS SOMETHING. Cell 1 runs the identical
fixture WITHOUT ownership and asserts the broker SURVIVES. So the suite is known to be able to
observe a leak, and cells 2 and 3 are not passing because brokers happen to die on their own.
Under this mutation cell 1 stays green and cells 2 and 3 flip, which is the discrimination.
IT MUST STILL TYPECHECK, because the suite's command builds nothing but tsx still type-strips and
`pnpm typecheck` covers this file. A const-asserted array with one member keeps every downstream
type intact, so the red that arrives is the assertion's own and not a compile error.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE, and it is asserted in the suite rather than left out. SIGKILL is
uncatchable: the handler never runs, the child handle dies with the process, and the broker is
orphaned regardless. Cell 5 asserts that leak as a fact and checks the orphan carries the minted
store-dir token, because that token is the only evidence a later reaper can match. Parentage
covers the case this helper fixes; the token covers the case it cannot. Neither covers both, and
a reader who takes this for a solved problem has been misled.

mutations.name: the terminating signals are no longer handled, so a killed suite orphans its broker again
